reviews.rationale: At the exact pinned source, _safe_path_segment sanitizes Artifact.type and Artifact.id before constructing artifact_dir, and sanitizes MountedArtifactContent.filename before writes beneath the per-turn host artifact root. The source-bound contract proves each helper result is a nonempty single relative component in the declared alphabet, including after trimming dot-only values. Exact-source replay and a source-weakened slash mutation ground-truth this narrow claim. The declared input trust is workspace configuration/artifact data; symlink ancestry, host_root provenance, races, collisions, attacker reachability, and current security impact are outside scope.

reviews.rationale: The workflow action does send the completed message to SMTP, but the regex does not independently provide the header-injection guarantee. In an exact CPython 3.12.15 replay of the pinned SAFE_EMAIL_PATTERN and _build_email_message AST, sender CR/LF injection raises during EmailMessage header construction; recipient CR/LF injection raises at the exact address check before the builder returns; and a trailing LF admitted by Python '$' is normalized by EmailMessage to the original single-line address with no extra Bcc header. The pinned send_email_smtp call invokes the builder before constructing SMTP/SMTP_SSL, so builder failures cannot reach the network sink. This is a composed standard-library and call-order behavior, not a useful regex-only security contract. No header-injection finding or impact is claimed. See email-header-replay.json.

reviews.pattern:
# Negative lookbehind - don't match if preceded by :, /, word char, or +
    # (+ prevents matching after subaddress in emails like user+tag@domain.com)
    # Note: @ is allowed so we can extract domains from emails like user@domain.com
    (?<![:/\w+])
    # Domain part - match at least one label + dot followed by TLD
    (?>                                  # Atomic group to prevent backtracking
        (?>                              # Atomic group for the repeating label + dot sequence
            (?:
                xn--[a-zA-Z0-9]+         # Punycode (IDN) label
                |                        # OR
                [a-zA-Z0-9]              # Regular domain label
                (?>[a-zA-Z0-9-]{0,61}    # Up to 61 alphanumeric or hyphen chars
                [a-zA-Z0-9])?            # Ending with alphanumeric (optional group)
            )
            \.                           # Followed by a dot
        )+                               # One or more label + dot sequences

        # TLD part - handle both regular and punycode TLDs
        (?:
            xn--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+            # Punycode TLD
            |                            # OR
            [a-zA-Z]{2,}                 # Regular TLD (at least 2 alpha chars)
        )
        # Optional additional TLDs (e.g., .co.uk)
        (?:\.
            (?:
                xn--[a-zA-Z0-9-]+        # Punycode TLD
                |                        # OR
                [a-zA-Z]{2,}             # Regular TLD
            )
        )*                               # Zero or more additional TLD components
    )
    # Negative lookahead - don't match if followed by :, /, word char, + or @
    # (+ and @ prevent matching local parts of email addresses)
    (?![:/\w+@])

reviews.rationale: The input scope strings can be requested by an MCP OAuth client and are carried through the pinned FastMCP OIDC proxy and Tracecat issuer, so the extracted UUIDs are only claimed identity context. The runtime authorization consumers do not grant from these regex matches: resolve_role_for_request checks the requested workspace against token scopes and then resolve_role checks database-derived org roles or explicit workspace membership; resolve_org_role_for_request intersects claimed IDs with active database memberships. list_user_workspaces also computes memberships first and uses claimed IDs only to narrow the result. The internal issuer signs an organization_id claim only after requiring exactly one organization membership; if a different client-requested org scope makes the Watchtower claim set ambiguous, its resolver intersects the claims with that user's database memberships before selecting an organization. The regexes are claim parsers, not authorization gates, and no separate regex-backed security property or privilege escalation is supported at this pin.

reviews.rationale: A narrow contract asks whether any key accepted by the exact pinned Python match language contains '='. Authenticated workflow configuration supplies run_python env_vars; the nsjail executor validates each non-PYTHONPATH key before adding it to env_map and passing it in --env arguments and the child process environment. POSIX requires environment names not to contain '='. The proof does not claim full POSIX name validity: Python '$' accepts one terminal LF, which is outside this contract. The same validator also protects ActionSandboxConfig env keys. No current bypass or impact is claimed because this property holds at the pinned source and subprocess also rejects '=' in environment keys.

reviews.rationale: The pattern is the shared Pydantic request-name validator for table and column creation. The authorized public create routes use TableCreate and TableColumnCreate; the internal table route reconstructs TableCreate and the internal column route uses TableColumnCreate. The exact service validates names again before dynamic DDL, and column DDL inserts names through quote_identifier. The request-level invariant that the double quote is excluded is useful as a defense-in-depth regression gate. Python `$` allows a final LF in the schema helper, but the service rejects it before DDL. No current SQL injection or security impact is claimed.
